body:
**Working entry (chk-ep3sqyx7, verbatim):** `viola adopt` — a plain `claude` session, by session-shaped id, closed and
resumed under an operator-given name and parent; the live-elsewhere refusal guards it.
**Freight:** none (the `pins` view lists no block on chk-ep3sqyx7; its `block` query returns 0 rows).

**Capability in reach:** v2-13 «Adopt a plain session into the fleet» (method `e2e`), requirement: `viola adopt --name [--parent

]` closes a session started outside viola and resumes it under viola with a name and its place in the fleet, built on `revive`, never taking over a running process's terminal, guarded by the live-elsewhere refusal. Acceptance: a plain claude session named by its session id ends and resumes under viola with the given name and parent and is then driven like any wrapped session; a session live in another claude is refused; no running process's terminal is taken over.

- A CLI verb `viola adopt` that takes a session-shaped id and an operator-given name (and optionally a parent), and
  starts a viola wrapper whose claude child resumes that session, so the session stands on the board as a named
  instance with its lineage, driven like any wrapped session.

- [inferred] Built on `revive`'s start path (`src/cmd/revive.rs`): the `--resume <id>` argv through
  `viola_agent_claude::resume_args`, the `claude agents --json` preflight and its closed `session-live` refusal, the
  start shared with `run`. What `adopt` reuses and what it adds is measured at P3.

- [inferred] The id's shape is checked by the existing closed session-id check before any home read beyond the strict
  ones, and a malformed id is refused with a closed word.

- [inferred] A session listed live by `claude agents --json` (the live-elsewhere read) is refused before any child is
  spawned; viola never takes over a running process's terminal.

- [inferred] What «closes a session started outside viola» means is a P3 measurement and a P3 fork: the conservative
  arm (directive item 3) is that `adopt` never ends or signals a process it did not start — it RESUMES only a session
  live nowhere, and refuses a live one with a hint to end it by hand. Any other arm is a boundary widening, the
  operator's (written to `founder-forks.md`, the conservative arm taken PROVISIONAL meanwhile).

- [inferred] The name and parent land as an instance's first snapshot and the lineage record the board reads; a
  second adopt of the same id, and an adopt onto a name already held, each have a defined closed outcome (P3).

- [inferred] The adopted session's cwd, model and effort have a defined source where no snapshot ever recorded them
  (P3 measures the candidates; a reading from another process is a possible crossing, named at P3).

- [inferred] Whether `adopt` opens a terminal (as `open` / `up`) or runs in the terminal it is typed in (as `revive`),
  and whether it is an MCP tool (conservative arm: CLI-only), are P3 forks.

- [inferred] CI on `e7703af0` (Setup 5a read: `e7703af09c0f verdict: green · checks 7/7 · attempt 2 · wall 1707 s ·
  runs ci#45361892176 completed/success`; the earlier attempt unread by the tool). Per the phase directive (overseer,
  measured 2026-11-24T09:34Z): attempt 1 of ci#45361892176 ran 4320 tests, 4319 passed, ONE killed at the 20 s line —
  `security_negatives_env_capture env_name_with_the_user_word_reads_fail_and_records_nothing`; its sibling
  `kept_name_reaches_no_stamp_or_record` passed at 16.9 s; no assertion failed; the commit changed no source file.
  Folded by the directive's word as this chunk's own item: say from the code and `.config/nextest.toml` what those
  two cases wait on and what they cost locally and under coverage, and give them a margin that holds on the runner by
  the tree's own form for a case that waits by design (its class or its work reduced — never the kill line raised for
  every test). Acceptance: a measured time per case against its kill, not a green run.

- Nothing live in this phase: no live start, no window, no key, no signal to a process viola did not start, no real
  session read, listed, ended, adopted or resumed, nothing of the operator's real `~/.claude*` read (directive).

- Every live reading of `adopt` (it ends a session of the operator's and spends real `claude` starts) is the operator's
  to grant; a clause the fakes cannot carry is planned GATED on it.

- Out of scope: the fleet console (Epoch 6), model/effort switching («Switching a session's model and effort»), and
  `viola up`'s reboot reading (R4b, «The fleet on the founder's host»).

# Phase directive — «`viola adopt`» (Epoch 5, viola-0.2.0; the head entry `chk-ep3sqyx7` at `e7703af0`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. A fact the plan needs and this directive does not state is
ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

**The operator is at WORK, reached only through the overseer**: raise NO question dialog for him. A fork that is his is written to
`{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the options in order with each one's cost, the recommendation marked);
his answer comes later through the overseer. **A boundary widening is never settled by a delegate:** it takes its
most conservative arm, marked PROVISIONAL, when the entry can be built whole on that arm — or the phase stops
there. A technical fork is answered by the overseer's relay at once. **This phase makes NO live start, opens,
moves, focuses or closes NO window, dispatches nothing, sends NO key, ends, closes, revives or resumes NO real session and sends no signal to any process it did not start, and reads nothing of the operator's real
`~/.claude*` — a `viola list` among them: on this host the board runs PATH's real `claude` unless none is
reachable.** In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-24T09:34Z — cite them as this directive's

- The tree at `e7703af0` = its upstream: position 134 records, 132 complete, 0 pending, 2 gated
  (`2026-11-24-viola-focus` on R3, `2026-11-24-viola-up` on R4a); coverage of viola-0.2.0 `verified 27/37 ·
  deferred 2 · planned 8 · unclaimed 6`. v2-07 is VERIFIED (R2 read green live). The route's next entry is
  `chk-ep3sqyx7` «`viola adopt`», its hint verbatim: «a plain `claude` session, by session-shaped id, closed and
  resumed under an operator-given name and parent; the live-elsewhere refusal guards it». It carries NO carry.
  The capability it can claim is v2-13 «Adopt a plain session into the fleet» (method `e2e`).
- **CI on `e7703af0` read RED once and green on its second attempt** (ci#45361892176): attempt 1 — 4320 tests,
  4319 passed, ONE killed at the 20 s line, `security_negatives_env_capture
  env_name_with_the_user_word_reads_fail_and_records_nothing`; its sibling `kept_name_reaches_no_stamp_or_record`

  configuration what those two cases wait on, what they cost locally and under coverage, and give them a margin
  that holds on the runner by the tree's own form for a case that waits by design (its class or its work
  reduced — never the kill line raised for every test); the witness is a measured time, not a green run.
- `hyprctl locked` read `true` at 09:34:17Z. Another project builds on this host: a gate red with no failed
  assertion is read against `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py
  read --from <UTC stamp> --to <UTC stamp>` first (two stamps: the tool refuses the word `now`) and never
  re-run for green; read `df -m /tmp` beside it.
- **The operator's real fleet runs on this host NOW**, and plain `claude` sessions of his beside it. Nothing of
  them is read, listed, ended, adopted or signalled by this phase. The operator's answers of 2026-11-24 on the
  three chunks before this one stand in the tree's own rows and sidecars; cite them from there.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry as it stands at `e7703af0`, v2-13 and the folded CI item, nothing wider. Say at P1,
   clause by clause of v2-13's acceptance, what «verified» can rest on HERE: which clauses the fakes prove (the
   id's shape check, the live-elsewhere refusal, the resume's argv, the name and parent recorded, the adopted
   instance driven by a send and a wait), and which need a real plain `claude` session ended and resumed. **A
   live `viola adopt` ENDS a session of the operator's and spends real `claude` starts: every live reading is his
   to grant — name each (which session it ends and how, how many starts, what it leaves, how it is undone) and
   plan the claim GATED on it where the fakes cannot carry a clause.**
2. **Measurements first, at P3, each a number or a closed word from a test, a no-start probe over a TEST home,
   the recorded fixtures or the code:** what `revive` and the board's agents read already give (the unwrapped
   rows, the session id's shape and where it is checked, `session-live` and its fail-open read); what «closes a
   session started outside viola» can mean without taking over a running process's terminal — which acts exist
   (none; a refusal telling the operator to end it; a signal to a pid; a resume beside it) and what each needs to
   know about a process viola did not start; what the real CLI does when one session id is resumed while its
   first process still runs (from the capability ledger's recorded rows only — if no row holds it, it is

   snapshot ever recorded them; what makes the name and parent land (a first snapshot, a `lineage` line) and
   what a second adopt of the same id does. Say what stays the fake's and unmeasured live.
3. **Forks, each with its options priced and marked his or technical:** the verb's argument surface; **whether
   `adopt` ever ends or signals a process it did not start** (a boundary widening — its conservative arm:
   `adopt` only RESUMES a session that is not live anywhere, and refuses a live one with a hint to end it by
   hand); whether it opens a terminal (as `open` / `up` do) or runs in the terminal it is typed in (as `revive`
   does); where the cwd comes from (the agents read, a flag, the caller's folder) and whether reading it from
   another process is a crossing; the closed words, exits, hints and output lines, each beside the existing
   tables; every new record, field or log line; every new time bound; whether it is an MCP tool (its
   conservative arm: CLI-only). **Say plainly whether one implement window holds the entry with the folded CI
   item, and if not, the split you would make — a split is his.**
4. **Read the playbook's escalate rows BEFORE the P3 block is written**, so that a boundary widening is named in
   the block's first lines, never found at P4. Search ALL seven masters by the counted literals a row or a test
   pins (the verb table, the help's rows, exit-cause tables, the seam's «product caller» wording, the time-bound
   lists) and by «never», «only», «replays no»; name every reached row with the read-not-reached beside them. The
   time-bound question was answered by the operator on 2026-11-24 (three rows of their own): a new bound on
   a new bearer lands as a row of its own beside the two list rows, which are not grown and not split.
5. **At P3's END, before P4:** ONE block in `founder-forks.md` — your window, the measurements, every reached
   row, each fork of his with the arm taken PROVISIONAL meanwhile, and whether the entry can be built whole on
   those arms. If it can, go on to P4 without waiting; if a fork of his has no conservative arm that builds, stop
   there and say so in one line.
6. Say what each new record writes to DISK, what outlives a SIGKILL, and what an `adopt` lets one session end,
   start, learn or change of another's.
7. Every `gate.py control` has an id of 1–16 characters, its `--timeout S`, and an entry filtered to its guard's
   own cases that builds the whole workspace where the case needs a root binary. Every filter term SELECTS at
   least one test under its layer flag once its step is built. An expect atom must be able to fail; a word that
   may honestly read two ways is a READING (`expect = []`); an after-read of state OTHER actors move is keyed to
   the round leg; no entry asserts a state a later step of the same plan ends. A test that skips prints why.
8. **Any live step the plan holds** names: what it needs ABSENT or PRESENT on disk outside the tree and the
   no-start entry that reads it; a script that closes what it opened on every exit path, found a second way when
   its first reading is empty; every inherited `VIOLA_*` name stripped; every board read with no `claude`
   reachable; a stand-in program that takes the arguments the wrapper puts first; and a rehearsal form that
   cannot reach a capped start or the operator's real sessions. It is fired only on the operator's own word.
9. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned
   user home. Read `df` before a whole rebuild. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission
   classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and tell the overseer. On an account-limit refusal, stop.
10. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool. End every process you start; remove no scratch clone by a recursive
    delete — name it on the card. Leaves hold no figure the code states.
11. Run the phase exactly as the letters say, read as they stand. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a
    tool printed it: the union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the
    union or its standing list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` /
    `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

body: - **start / collision_check / refused / checked_exe / open_wrapper_log / pump_child** (`src/cmd/run.rs`) — callers in `src/cmd/run.rs` (`run`, `refused_with`), `src/cmd/revive.rs` and `src/cmd/up.rs`; reused unchanged by `adopt`, so no signature changes and no caller threading.
- **resume_args** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs`) — callers `src/cmd/revive.rs` and `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs:206`; reused unchanged.
- **read_here** (`src/run/agents.rs:113`) — callers `src/cmd/revive.rs` (`live_elsewhere`) and the board; reused unchanged.

- **A start is a `Launch` handed to `start`** (`src/cmd/run.rs:253`, `src/cmd/revive.rs:254`): a verb builds program, args, spawn dir, lineage and pair, and `start` does the rest — the collision check, pin, gate, bind, trust step, first snapshot, `lineage` and `launch` lines, spawn.
- **Preflight readings in a fixed order, the first refusal winning** (`src/cmd/revive.rs:191-208`), unit-tested by a case table over closures (`src/cmd/revive.rs:423-482`).
- **A refusal is a closed `detail` plus a fixed pair, or under `--json` one document** (`src/cmd/revive.rs:76-124`, `client::refused_document`).

- **The resume id crosses only as one argv element built by `resume_args`** (`src/cmd/revive.rs:251`), of the closed session-id shape (`is_session_id`, `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:138`), checked by clap's value parser (`src/cmd/revive.rs:57-63`).
- **Strict check before the log**: `trusted` then `checked_exe` before `open_wrapper_log` (`src/cmd/revive.rs:155-178`).
- **A refusal's pair names no id, path or pid** (`src/cmd/revive.rs:88-90`).
- **A test that runs a verb looking up `claude` puts the fake first on PATH** (testing.md 2026-10-10); session-live reads over `plant_agents` (`tests/cli_revive.rs:398-421`).
- **Every verify-driven test is in the `verify_window_` class** (`tests/support/verify.rs:564`).
- **A verb added to `viola --help` joins the `HELP` literal and the served list** (testing.md 2026-11-24).
- `src/cmd/adopt.rs` — the `adopt` verb: args, the closed checks and readings, the `Launch` handed to `run`'s `start`, its unit cases
- `tests/cli_adopt.rs` — the booted cases over the fake agent: adopted under a name and parent, driven by a send and a wait, refused when listed live, refusals and documents
- `scripts/r5-adopt.sh` — the gated live reading, with its rehearsal form over the fake agent
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — the `Adopt` verb, its dispatch, and `adopt` in the help's `setup:` row
- `src/main.rs` — `adopt` read as the wrapper's named role, its case rows
- `src/cmd/revive.rs` — `live_elsewhere` and the session-id value parser shared with `adopt`
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` — the `HELP` literal and the served list
- `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` — `adopt`'s exit-1 causes and its hint
- `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` — `adopt`'s refusal document writer named
- `tests/security_negatives_env_capture.rs` — the two verify-driven cases renamed into the `verify_window_` class

- `env_name_with_the_user_word_reads_fail_and_records_nothing|kept_name_reaches_no_stamp_or_record` over the tree (`git grep -n`, sealed parquet aside): 2 hits · 2 changed (the definitions) · 0 no-change.

- `verify_window_` over `tests scripts .config crates` (`git grep -c`): 25 hits in 10 files · 0 changed · 25 no-change (the class's filter and notes name the prefix, never a case list; `tests/contract_lints.rs:130` pins the filter line, unchanged).

- `revive` in the masters' verb rows (`rec.py find --text "open, run, revive, up"` over the seven): 4 rows · 0 changed here · 4 no-change at phase (`design-system · contract/help-output/verb-groups`, `contract/viola-help/verb-groups`; `layout-templates · contract/cli-verbs/help`, `contract/viola-help/verb-groups` — the wrap's amendments).

- **What revive and the board already give.** `claude agents --json` lists live sessions only (`AgentsRow` holds a pid and status, `src/run/agents.rs`), so an unwrapped row stands on the board only while its session runs; `is_session_id` is the one shape check (clap value parser on revive's `--id`, `src/cmd/revive.rs:57`); `session-live` is revive's preflight reading 3 of 4, skipped under `--fork`, passing on a failed read (`src/cmd/revive.rs:210-215, 244`).

- **«Closes a session started outside viola».** Acts that exist in viola today: none ends a process it did not start (`.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-10-10; security-plan: `viola focus` and `open` never act on a window they did not open). Candidates: (a) none — refuse a live id with a hint to end it by hand; (b) a signal to the agents row's `pid`, which needs the pid, its start time (`startedAt`) against pid reuse, the same user, and a way to know the session ended cleanly; (c) a resume beside it. The agents row is the only source viola has about such a process.

- **A second resume while the first process runs.** No capability-ledger row holds it: UNMEASURED by the ledger. The architecture row `decision/revive-refuses-live-session` states, as its why, «A second claude --resume of a held id is neither refused nor copied by the CLI: both sessions run under one id, two writers on one transcript» — a master's statement, not a ledger row.

- **cwd, model and effort with no snapshot.** No viola record exists for a plain session. cwd: an agents row's `cwd` exists only while the session is live, which is exactly when `adopt` refuses it; the measured ledger row `resume-session` resumes in a folder other than the session's own (Run E's own dir, `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs:203`), recorded on 2.1.328 (`fixtures/claude/2.1.328/SessionStart.resume-1.json`); 2.1.330's stamp is not read here. So the caller's folder (as `run`), or a flag, needs no read from another process. Model and effort: `--model` / `--effort` given, else the config default (`run::launch::read_default`, `src/cmd/run.rs:441`), as on `run`.

- **What lands the name and parent.** `start` writes the first snapshot with `lineage` and the `lineage` line after `wheel` (`src/cmd/run.rs:708-745`); `lineage_of` takes `--parent` or the inherited `VIOLA_NAME`. A second `adopt` of an id whose adopted instance is live: the agents read lists its child (the fake lists live wrapped agents), so `session-live`; of a dead one: it passes. An `adopt` onto a name held live or stale: `run`'s collision check (`already-live`, `stale-heartbeat`); onto a dead name: `start` reuses it as `run` does.

- **What stays the fake's, unmeasured live:** a real plain `claude` session (started outside viola, in its own folder) ended and resumed under viola from another folder on the host's CLI; the real agents read listing a real live session.

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-24-viola-adopt · **Version:** viola-0.2.0
- **Base:** e7703af09c0ff2dddf32cc858a03e3af4bea5d0b (HEAD at P4)
- **Directive:** the overseer's phase directive, `inputs#I1`

- **Forks:** `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-24T09-38-18Z-phase/founder-forks.md` Block 1. W1, W2 and W3 are his, each on
  its arm 1 PROVISIONAL. R5 is his live reading and gates v2-13. T1–T6 are technical, each on its lean, the
  overseer's relay owed.

`viola adopt --name [--parent

]` brings a plain `claude` session — started outside viola and already ended — into the fleet. It starts a viola wrapper in the terminal it is typed in, whose claude child resumes that session (`--resume `, one argv element of a direct spawn). The session then stands on the board under the given name and parent and is driven like any wrapped session. `adopt` is `revive`'s start without a log to read: the id comes from the operator, in the closed session-id shape. The live-elsewhere reading `revive` makes (`claude agents --json`, a listed id refused `session-live`, a failed read passing) guards it, so a session still running anywhere is never resumed a second time, and viola ends, signals and takes over no process it did not start (W1 arm 1). Every other step is `run`'s own start, unchanged: collision check, pin, version gate, bind, automatic verify, trust step, first snapshot with `lineage` and `launch`, spawn (architecture · decision/revive-refuses-live-session; security-plan · decision/session-id-argv-no-shell; architecture · decision/lineage-label-only).

The chunk also folds the CI kill of `e7703af0`, attempt 1 (`inputs#I1`; research §Folded CI item). Two
`security_negatives_env_capture` cases each run one whole `viola verify --record`, but neither carries the
`verify_window_` prefix under which `tests/support/verify.rs:564` puts every verify-driven test. Each therefore took
its binary's 20 s kill (measured 20.013 s, killed, and 16.907 s under CI coverage). They move into their class; no
kill line moves.

What this chunk does not do: open a terminal or run a window step (T2), serve `adopt` as an MCP tool (W3), read
anything from another process beyond the existing agents read (T3), or end a session (W1). The real-CLI clause of
v2-13 waits on R5, the operator's live reading.

1. **`src/cmd/adopt.rs` — the arguments** (T1). `AdoptArgs` (clap): the positional session id through a
   session-id value parser — the same one revive's `--id` uses, moved to `pub(super)` (step 6). Then `--name`
   (required, `send::parse_name`), `--parent` (optional, `send::parse_name`), `--model` (`run::parse_model`),
   `--effort` (`run::parse_effort`) and `--json`. There is no `last = true` word list, so any word after `--` is a
   clap usage error. `checked` refuses a `--parent` equal to `--name` as a usage exit 2 with a fixed line naming
   neither value, as `run`'s does (`src/cmd/run.rs:113-119`). Unit cases: `adopt_args_take_an_id_a_name_a_parent_and_a_pair`
   and the labelled rstest table `adopt_args_refuse_as_usage`:
   - parses: the id, the name, the parent, the pair;
   - exit 2: an id of another shape, an id in upper case, an id written as an option word (`--id=--danger…` form,
     as `src/cmd/revive.rs:746`), a name that is no name, a missing `--name`, a parent equal to the name, a bad
     model, a bad effort, a word after `--`.
   (keeps tests S5, a11y S2)

2. **`src/cmd/adopt.rs` — the refusals.** `adopt`'s `Refusal` holds `StrictModes` and `SessionLive`, each with a
   closed `detail` (`strict-modes-failed` · `session-live`) and a fixed pair:
   - `StrictModes` → `human::instance_state_pair(name)`;
   - `SessionLive` → `unable: that session is open in another claude` / `hint: close it there first, then adopt it
     again`.

   No pair holds the id, a path or a pid (security-plan · decision/refusals-hold-no-paths-pids-ids). Under `--json`
   each is `client::refused_document(detail)`. The run-shared refusals (`already-live`, `stale-heartbeat`,
   `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `squatted-name`, `socket-dir-refused`) stay `run`'s own, written by its `collision_check`
   and `refused_with`. A unit case pins each pair and detail by literal and asserts no hint names `release`.
   (keeps design S2–S4, layouts S2)

3. **`src/cmd/adopt.rs` — the order.** `adopt(home, args)` mirrors `revive::started`:
   1. `trusted` — `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`, before any log. A refusal is
      `StrictModes`, exit 1, nothing opened.
   2. `checked_exe` — under `--json` its refusal is the `strict-modes-failed` document, else `refuse_tree`.
   3. `open_wrapper_log` (role `run`, `run-<name>.ndjson`).
   4. The preflight, in a fixed order with the first refusal winning:
      - the name's holder, through `run`'s `collision_check` over one `read_snapshot_or_replay`;
      - the live-elsewhere reading, the shared `live_elsewhere(home, cwd, id)` from step 6, refused `SessionLive`
        (one `process-exit{detail:"session-live"}` through `run::refused`).

      Like revive's `preflight_order`, it is a small generic fn of two closures, with unit cases
      `adopt_preflight_order_the_first_refusal_wins` (a table: the pass, holder alone, live alone, both) and
      `adopt_preflight_order_a_refused_holder_takes_no_agents_read`.
   5. On a pass, `Launch` goes to `run::start` and then `pump_child`, as revive's does. `Launch` holds:
      - `program` `PROGRAM`, `args` `resume_args(id, false)`;
      - `spawn_dir` the current dir (T3);
      - `json`;
      - `lineage` `{parent, role: None}`, with `parent` = `--parent`, else the inherited `client::own_name()` unless
        it equals `--name` (as `run::lineage_of`, `src/cmd/run.rs:135`; a small fn of its own here, so
        `src/cmd/run.rs` is not touched);
      - `given` `(model, effort)`;
      - `window` `None`.

   An anyhow error before `pump_child` prints the `internal-error` document under `--json` and returns the error, as
   `revive` does (`src/cmd/revive.rs:143-147`). It adds no event kind, log line, span field, record, time bound or
   env read. Unit cases: the lineage fn's four arms (given; inherited; inherited equal to the name, dropped; none).

4. **`src/cmd/mod.rs` — the verb.**
   - `mod adopt;` and `Command::Adopt(adopt::AdoptArgs)`, dispatched as `Command::Revive`'s start arm is.
   - The help's `setup:` row becomes `setup:    open, run, revive, adopt, up, verify, plugin install`. Verb-group
     order: after `revive`, the verb it is built on (design-system · contract/help-output/verb-groups; S1).

5. **`src/main.rs` — the role.** The word `adopt` is the wrapper's named role (`Role::Other`), as `revive`'s start
   is, so its catch site stays silent (architecture · decision/silent-roles-at-internal-error-catch). Case rows:
   `adopt` alone, after `--home`, after `--home=`, and a later `adopt` word (`send adopt`, `Role::Cli`).

6. **`src/cmd/revive.rs` — the shared readers.** `parse_session_id` and `live_elsewhere` become `pub(super)`, with no
   change to their bodies. No caller of `revive` moves (research §Graph impact).

7. **`tests/cli_adopt.rs` — the booted cases, over the fake agent as `claude` first on PATH, each in its own stamped
   home** (S1, S2, S6; testing.md 2026-10-10):
   - `adopt_resumes_the_session_under_its_name_and_parent`: `viola adopt <ANOTHER_SESSION> --name builder --parent
     overseer` (the fake planted with a turn script through its `fake-args` file). Asserts:
     - the log's start records `wheel` → `lineage{parent:"overseer", role:null}` → `launch`, then a `session-start`
       with cause `resume` and `agent_session_id` the given id;
     - the snapshot's `lineage.parent` is `overseer` and its `cwd` the typed-in folder;
     - the fake's receipt holds `--resume` and the id as two arguments.

     Then one `viola send builder` (stdin) reads back, and `viola wait builder` reads its `turn-ended`
     (the «driven like any wrapped session» clause).
   - `adopt_spawns_its_own_child_in_its_own_terminal`: the snapshot's `child_pid` names a process whose parent is the
     wrapper's pid (`/proc/<pid>/stat`), and the wrapper's controlling terminal is the test's outer PTY. This is the
     «no running process's terminal is taken over» clause, by construction.
   - `adopt_of_a_session_open_in_another_claude_is_session_live`: `plant_agents(home, None, &listed(id))`. Expects
     exit 1, stdout empty, stderr exactly adopt's pair with the hint last, one `process-exit{detail:"session-live"}`,
     one `agents-probe` pair holding no id, no child start (the receipt's start count unchanged), and every new line
     schema-valid.
   - `adopt_json_of_a_listed_session_is_the_session_live_document`: exactly
     `{"v":1,"error":"session-live","detail":null}`, stderr empty.
   - `adopt_of_the_id_a_live_adopted_instance_holds_is_session_live`: a first adopt live, then a second adopt of the
     same id under another name is refused `session-live` (the fake lists live wrapped agents).
   - `adopt_whose_agents_read_fails_starts` (rstest cases `malformed` · `oversize`): it starts, with one
     `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json"}`.
   - `adopt_onto_a_live_name_prints_the_run_collision_pair` (booted_wrapper) and its `--json` `already-live` document.
   - `adopt_refuses_state_another_user_could_write` (the home and the instance dir, each widened through
     `support::home::widen`): exit 1, the instance pair (under `--json` the `strict-modes-failed` document), no log
     opened, and the mode left as found.
   - `adopt_with_a_malformed_id_is_a_usage_error`: exit 2, and the home not created.

   No test sends a signal to a process it did not start; each started wrapper is tied (S2) and stopped in its guard.
   (keeps tests S1–S9, obs S3 and S5, security S1)

8. **`tests/cli_output_plain.rs`.** The `HELP` literal's `setup:` line and `help_lists_only_served_verbs`' served
   list gain `adopt` (testing.md 2026-11-24).

9. **`tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` and `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`.**
   - `cross_exit_causes`: adopt's exit-1 causes join the table — `session-live` with adopt's own hint constant,
     `strict-modes-failed`, and `already-live` through `run`'s pair. Each is a code word, no hint names `release`,
     and `no_two_codes_share_a_hint` stays green: if that test keys hints by code alone, adopt's `session-live` row is
     keyed by verb and code, and the test's reading is extended rather than its oracle relaxed.
   - `contract_error_bodies`: a row naming `src/cmd/adopt.rs`'s refusal document writer and its witness
     `adopt_json_of_a_listed_session_is_the_session_live_document`. `product_error_writers_are_each_named` stays green.

10. **`tests/security_negatives_env_capture.rs` — the folded CI item** (T6). Rename
    `kept_name_reaches_no_stamp_or_record` → `verify_window_kept_name_reaches_no_stamp_or_record`, and
    `env_name_with_the_user_word_reads_fail_and_records_nothing` →
    `verify_window_env_name_with_the_user_word_reads_fail_and_records_nothing`. Bodies are unchanged. Each now takes
    the `verify_window_` override, which stands first in `.config/nextest.toml`: `ci` 20 s × 4, `mutants` 20 s × 4.
    The binary's other three cases keep the 20 s kill. No kill line moves, and `.config/nextest.toml` is untouched
    (`tests/contract_lints.rs:130` pins the class filter line, unchanged). Implement records, in
    `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-24-viola-adopt/evidence/ci-fold.md`, each case's measured local time from entry
    7's log against its 80 s kill.

11. **The CI-under-coverage witness of step 10** (the operator pass, outside the block). After the pre-CI push's run
    reads green (entry 18), the pass downloads that run's `junit-ubuntu-latest` artifact (`gh api
    repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/artifacts`, then the artifact's zip, into a fresh scratch dir). It reads the two
    renamed cases' `time` and appends one line per case to `evidence/ci-fold.md`:
    `ci-fold: <case> <seconds> s of 80 s under coverage, ci#<id>`. Entry 19 reads those lines.

12. **`scripts/r5-adopt.sh` — the live reading R5 and its rehearsal** (item 8 of `inputs#I1`).
    - **Forms:**
      - `r5-adopt.sh <base> <viola> <home> a <id>`, the R5a arm: adopt a real ended plain session;
      - `r5-adopt.sh <base> <viola> <home> b <id>`, the R5b arm: a real live one is refused;
      - `r5-adopt.sh <base> <viola> --rehearse`, both arms over the fake agent.
    - **Preconditions:** `<base>` must be ABSENT (refused if it stands); `<id>` must pass the session-id shape (a
      `grep -Ex` on the shape, else exit 2). Live arms only: `claude` is read present on PATH by `command -v`, with
      no start.
    - **Environment:** every inherited `VIOLA_*` name is unset before anything starts. Every board read
      (`viola --home <home> list --json`) runs with `PATH` set to an empty dir the script makes, so no `claude` is
      reachable from it.
    - **R5a:** `viola --home <home> adopt <id> --name adopt-probe --parent r5-parent` runs from `<base>/typed-in`
      inside a pseudo-terminal of the script's own (util-linux `script -qfec`, its input held open by a FIFO the
      script owns). The script waits on the instance's `events.ndjson` for the `session-start` line, within a bound
      under 120 s. It reads the snapshot's `lineage.parent` and the line's `cause` and `agent_session_id`, sends one
      compiled prompt through `viola send adopt-probe` (stdin), and waits up to 300 s through `viola wait`. It then
      ends the wrapper it started: SIGTERM to the pid `script`'s child reports, found a second way through the
      snapshot's `pid` when the first reading is empty, each acted on only while `/proc/<pid>/exe` is the given
      `<viola>`.
    - **R5b:** `viola --home <home> adopt <id> --name adopt-live --json` reads `session-live`, exit 1, and no
      `adopt-live` child (no `child_pid` recorded).
    - **Teardown:** a `trap` on EXIT, INT and TERM ends every process the script started and nothing else. Nothing is
      removed recursively: the base is named on stdout for the operator.
    - **Verdict lines** (the plan's closed set; verification-harness.md 2026-11-24):
      - `r5a: <green|red> resumed=<yes|no> lineage=<yes|no> turn=<ended|none|unfired>`;
      - `r5b: <green|red> refused=<session-live|<code>|none> started=<none|child>`.
    - **Rehearsal:** builds a fake-only PATH (`<base>/bin` holding a copy of `target/debug/viola-fake-agent` as
      `claude`, then `/usr/bin:/bin` alone, so mise's `claude` is unreachable). It stamps its own `<base>/home` with
      `viola verify` against that fake under a test-owned user home and runtime dir, as the harness boot does
      (verification-harness.md §boot). It plants the fake's `fake-args` for a turn end, and for R5b `agents-rows.json`
      listing the minted id. It runs both arms and prints both lines, then `r5: rehearsed — not a live reading` last.
      It cannot reach a real `claude` or the operator's sessions.

13. **R5 itself** (the operator pass, on his word only, at his host, unlocked). `cargo build -p viola` (entry 20)
    builds the release-shaped binary. Then:
    - entry 21 (R5a), with `R5_HOME` and `R5_ID` exported: his home choice and the id of the plain session he started
      and ended himself;
    - entry 22 (R5b), with `R5_ID` the id of a plain session he leaves running.

    Each verdict line is copied by the operator into `evidence/r5.md`, which entry 14 reads. The home is his choice
    (Block 1, R5a): his stamped `~/.viola` adds no verify starts and leaves `adopt-probe` on his board; a fresh scratch
    home spends the automatic verify's starts.
- `src/cmd/adopt.rs` — the verb: arguments, refusals, preflight order, the `Launch` handed to `run::start`, unit cases
- `tests/cli_adopt.rs` — the booted cases over the fake agent
- `scripts/r5-adopt.sh` — R5's two live arms and their rehearsal
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — `Command::Adopt`, its dispatch, the help's `setup:` row
- `src/main.rs` — `adopt` as the wrapper's named role, its case rows
- `src/cmd/revive.rs` — `parse_session_id` and `live_elsewhere` shared, bodies unchanged
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` — the `HELP` literal and the served list
- `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` — adopt's exit-1 causes and hint
- `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` — adopt's refusal document writer
- `tests/security_negatives_env_capture.rs` — two cases renamed into the `verify_window_` class
**What the block runs, in order:**
1. The formatter and the linter.
2. The root binaries' units, then the adopt unit cases filtered.
3. The new integration cases by their prefix.
4. The readers of the moved literals and tables.
5. The folded binary under the `ci` profile.
6. The R5 script's parse and its rehearsal.
7. The host read.
8. The harness's three layers.
9. The gated reading.
10. The operator pass.
**What is not run, and why:**

- No `round` or `live` entry: R5 is the operator's act, fired once on his word through the `operator` entries 20–22,
  never by implement (`inputs#I1` items 1 and 8).

- No boot smoke: no boot-path file changes. `src/cmd/run.rs` and `src/run/` are untouched, and `adopt` hands
  `run::start` a `Launch` as `revive` does (research §Files to modify).
- No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 9).
- No fuzz target: no new parser.
- No `cargo deny`: no dependency edge moves.
**Must-pass readings owed to implement:**

- Entry 9 asserts literals step 12's script prints. Its first firing after the script exists, before any graded use,
  is the reading of entries 9, 21 and 22: the rehearsal prints the same verdict lines the live arms do.

- Entry 7's atoms are the renamed cases' names and nextest's summary. They are read from the local run archived at
  `target/run-archive/641`, whose summary line reads `5 tests run: 5 passed, 0 skipped`.
**Records made outside the block:**
- Entry 14 reads `evidence/r5.md`, which the operator writes from R5's output (step 13).
- Entry 19 reads `evidence/ci-fold.md`'s coverage lines, which the operator pass appends (step 11).
Neither entry carries an `artifact`.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each runs
`--timeout 900` against its own filtered entry, which reaches its case past fail-fast by `--no-fail-fast`. Each case
fails on its own bounded assertion, so a `timeout` reading would NOT read the guard as held.

| `adopt-shape` | `src/cmd/adopt.rs` | the session-id value parser on the positional id (a plain `String`) | `adopt_with_a_malformed_id_is_a_usage_error` | 5 |

body:
- (product) `viola adopt --name --parent

` starts a wrapper whose claude child resumes ``. The log holds `wheel` → `lineage{parent:p}` → `launch` → `session-start{cause:"resume", agent_session_id:}`, and the snapshot's `lineage.parent` is `p`. One `viola send` and one `viola wait` drive it to `turn-ended`. Witness: `adopt_resumes_the_session_under_its_name_and_parent` (architecture · contract/event-data/lineage; architecture · contract/child-argv/resume).

- (security) A session id listed by `claude agents --json` is refused `session-live`, exit 1, with adopt's fixed
  pair and no child, and the `adopt-live` control holds. A failed agents read starts. A second `adopt` of the id a
  live adopted instance holds is refused. Witnesses: `adopt_of_a_session_open_in_another_claude_is_session_live`,
  `adopt_json_of_a_listed_session_is_the_session_live_document`,
  `adopt_of_the_id_a_live_adopted_instance_holds_is_session_live`, `adopt_whose_agents_read_fails_starts`
  (architecture · decision/revive-refuses-live-session).

- (security) The id crosses only in the closed session-id shape, as one argv element of a direct spawn. A malformed
  id is a usage exit 2 before anything is read, and the `adopt-shape` control holds. Witnesses:
  `adopt_with_a_malformed_id_is_a_usage_error`, `adopt_args_refuse_as_usage` (security-plan ·
  decision/session-id-argv-no-shell; W2 arm 1, PROVISIONAL).

- (security) `adopt` spawns its own child in its own PTY and acts on no other process: witness
  `adopt_spawns_its_own_child_in_its_own_terminal` (W1 arm 1, PROVISIONAL).

- (security) A home or instance dir another user could write is refused before any log, exit 1, its mode left as
  found. Witness: `adopt_refuses_state_another_user_could_write` (security-plan ·
  decision/state-tree-strict-modes-before-use).

- (cli) Each refusal is one fixed pair, or under `--json` one clean document. `viola --help` lists `setup:    open,
  run, revive, adopt, up, verify, plugin install`. Tables green: `cli_output_plain`, `cross_exit_causes`,
  `contract_error_bodies` (design-system · contract/help-output/verb-groups; layout-templates ·
  contract/viola-help/verb-groups).

- (ci) Both verify-driven `security_negatives_env_capture` cases stand in the `verify_window_` class.
  `evidence/ci-fold.md` holds each one's measured time against its 80 s kill: locally from entry 7, and under
  coverage from the pre-CI push's green run (entry 19, step 11). No kill line moved.
- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit`, `run --integration` and `run --e2e` each print `"ok":true`.

- **`matrix#v2-13`** — GATED on R5. A plain claude session named by its session id ends and resumes under viola with
  the given name and parent, and is then driven like any wrapped session: read as `r5a: green resumed=yes lineage=yes
  turn=ended`. A session live in another claude is refused: read as `r5b: green refused=session-live started=none`.
  Both lines are in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-24-viola-adopt/evidence/r5.md`, read by entry 14. No running
  process's terminal is taken over: by construction, `adopt` resuming only a session live nowhere (W1 arm 1,
  PROVISIONAL), and witnessed over the fakes now. A stand-in, stub or recorded artifact never verifies the gated part.

- Rows: architecture · decision/revive-refuses-live-session, decision/lineage-label-only,
  decision/launch-pair-handed-not-verified, decision/silent-roles-at-internal-error-catch,
  decision/agents-listing-never-errors, decision/cli-flag-and-subcommand-style, contract/child-argv/resume,
  contract/claude-child-argv/resume, contract/event-data/lineage, contract/instance-snapshot/lineage,
  contract/cli-json-output/revive-refusal-codes, contract/cli-json-error-document/shape; security-plan ·
  decision/session-id-argv-no-shell, decision/refusals-hold-no-paths-pids-ids,
  decision/state-tree-strict-modes-before-use; design-system · contract/help-output/verb-groups; layout-templates ·
  contract/viola-help/verb-groups, contract/cli-verbs/help; obs-plan · contract/strict-modes-refusal-exit/1.
- Standing: tests S1–S9; obs S1, S3, S5; security S1, S4; design S1–S4; layouts S1–S2; a11y S2.

- Research files inspected: `src/cmd/revive.rs`, `src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/run/agents.rs`,
  `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/agents.rs`, `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`,
  `tests/support/start.rs`, `tests/cli_revive.rs`, `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`, `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`,
  `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`, `tests/security_negatives_env_capture.rs`, `tests/support/verify.rs`,
  `.config/nextest.toml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

- Code-graph: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-24T09-38-18Z-phase/tree-query-2026-11-24-viola-adopt.json` (start ·
  collision_check · refused · checked_exe · open_wrapper_log · pump_child @ `src/cmd/run.rs`, callers in run.rs,
  revive.rs, up.rs; resume_args callers revive.rs and verify/typed/runs.rs:206).
- Ending or signalling the plain session's process — viola acts on no process it did not start (W1 arm 1).

- Resuming beside a running session — two writers on one transcript (architecture ·
  decision/revive-refuses-live-session, its why).

- Reading the session's cwd, model or effort from its transcript, `~/.claude` or another process — no read beyond the
  existing agents read (T3).
- A `--cwd` flag or a window step — T2 and T3 keep `adopt` to the typed-in terminal and folder.
- An MCP `adopt` tool — W3 arm 1.
- Editing `src/cmd/run.rs` to share `lineage_of` — adopt keeps its own four-arm fn, so the boot path stays untouched.

- Raising `security_negatives_env_capture`'s 20 s binary kill, or the default — the class rename is the tree's form
  (testing.md 2026-09-28).
- Words after `--` — `adopt` passes nothing to the child beyond `--resume <id>` and the start's own flags.

- `viola run <name> -- claude --resume <id>` already reaches the same start unchecked (research §Measurements). `adopt`
  is that start with the id's shape, the live-elsewhere guard and the lineage, and so adds no crossing beyond what
  W2 names.

- A second adopt of the id a dead adopted instance held passes, and two instances' logs then hold one id. That is as
  designed (T4's reading); a later `revive` of either is guarded by the same agents read.

- The adopted instance records its launch pair like every start (`launch` line), which «Switching a session's model and
  effort» and v2-30 read later; this chunk claims neither.

- **Expected amendments (wrap):**

    contract/help-output/verb-groups, contract/viola-help/verb-groups).
  - layout-templates §Surface: cli — the same (layout-templates · contract/cli-verbs/help,
    contract/viola-help/verb-groups).
  - architecture §Standard Contracts — `adopt`'s `--json` refusal codes, a row beside
    contract/cli-json-output/revive-refusal-codes. An adopted start adds `--resume <id>`, a row beside
    contract/child-argv/resume.
  - architecture §Established Decisions — adopt refuses a session a live claude holds, a row beside
    decision/revive-refuses-live-session. adopt's start joins decision/silent-roles-at-internal-error-catch's named
    list.
  - security-plan — the operator-typed id source on the child's argv (W2, PROVISIONAL, his word owed). adopt's start
    joins the named lists of decision/state-tree-strict-modes-before-use, decision/home-tree-strict-modes-before-log,
    decision/exec-commands-absolute-pinned-path and decision/no-writes-under-claude-home. W1's no-signal arm is
    recorded as a row of its own (PROVISIONAL).
  - obs-plan — contract/strict-modes-refusal-exit/1 and decision/home-tree-check-before-log-init gain adopt's start.
    `adopt` logs as process `run`.
  - test-plan — contract/cli-human/internal-error's silent list gains adopt's start; tests/cli_adopt.rs named among
    the integration binaries.
  - a11y-plan — contract/start-refusal/home-strict-modes, contract/start-refusal/socket-dir,
    decision/strict-modes-refusal-before-any-write and contract/json-fault/internal-error gain adopt's start.
  - Each boundary widening (W1, W2, W3) carries pattern `rul-r74hshif` / `rul-p2zl2kgl` and its answerer: `delegate
    phase builder (conservative arm, PROVISIONAL)` until his own word.

   closed `detail` (`strict-modes-failed` · `session-live`) and a fixed pair:

title: I2-relay-1.md.txt
body: review — T1-T6: each its lean. Two things in R5, then card 2. (1) adopt holds the terminal it is typed in: say what hosts it in scripts/r5-adopt.sh (which pty or terminal, opened by what, closed how on every exit path) and that the LIVE path and the --rehearse path host it by the same code, so the rehearsal reads the hosting too. (2) Name in R5a the one prompt text and the model and effort the resumed start takes (the cheapest that proves a turn), and what that turn spends; both as parameters of his grant beside the home.

row.path: message: the overseer, delegate for the operator, in this session
row.why: review of p5-card-1: T1-T6 each on its lean; R5 hosting named and shared with the rehearsal; R5a prompt, model, effort and spend as grant parameters

body:
12. **`scripts/r5-adopt.sh` — the live reading R5 and its rehearsal** (item 8 of `inputs#I1`).
    - **Forms:**
      - `r5-adopt.sh <base> <viola> <home> a <id>`, the R5a arm: adopt a real ended plain session;
      - `r5-adopt.sh <base> <viola> <home> b <id>`, the R5b arm: a real live one is refused;
      - `r5-adopt.sh <base> <viola> --rehearse`, both arms over the fake agent.
    - **Preconditions:** `<base>` must be ABSENT (refused if it stands); `<id>` must pass the session-id shape (a
      `grep -Ex` on the shape, else exit 2). Live arms only: `claude` is read present on PATH by `command -v`, with
      no start.
    - **Environment:** every inherited `VIOLA_*` name is unset before anything starts. Every board read
      (`viola --home <home> list --json`) runs with `PATH` set to an empty dir the script makes, so no `claude` is
      reachable from it.
    - **The host of `adopt`'s terminal (`inputs#I2` (1)).** `adopt` holds the terminal it is typed in, so the script
      hosts it in a pseudo-terminal of its own. ONE function, `host_adopt`, does this; the live arms and `--rehearse`
      call the same function, and differ only in `PATH` and the home, so the rehearsal reads the hosting too.
      - **The pty:** util-linux `script -qfec <cmd> /dev/null` (`/usr/bin/script`, util-linux 2.42.4 on the host),
        started by `host_adopt` as a background child of the script. `-e` hands back the child's exit code; `-f`
        flushes; `/dev/null` keeps no typescript.
        - `<cmd>` is the `viola --home <home> adopt …` argv. Each word is quoted by `printf %q`, and the id has
          passed the shape check first. `SHELL=/bin/sh` is set for that call, since `script -c` runs its command
          through `$SHELL -c`.
        - The pty's input is a FIFO `<base>/pty-in`, which the script makes (`mkfifo`) and holds open for writing
          on its own fd 3 (`exec 3>`) before it starts `script`. The wrapper therefore never reads end-of-input, and
          no key is ever written to it.
        - `host_adopt` records `script`'s pid (`$!`) at its own start.
      - **Closed how, on every exit path** — one `close_host`, run by the `trap` on EXIT, INT and TERM and by the
        normal end alike, acting only on pids this run recorded:
        1. The wrapper's pid, read from the adopted instance's snapshot `pid`. As a second way when that read is
           empty, the one child of the recorded `script` pid whose `/proc/<pid>/exe` is the given `<viola>`.
           SIGTERM, acted on only while `/proc/<pid>/exe` is `<viola>`; the wrapper's claude child ends with its
           PTY.
        2. SIGTERM to the recorded `script` pid.
        3. Each waited for up to 10 s, then SIGKILL to the same pid while it is still the same process (its
           `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time, read at record, unchanged).
        4. Close fd 3, then remove the FIFO, one named file, never a recursive delete.

        A refused adopt (R5b) exits by itself, and `close_host` then finds both pids gone and acts on nothing. The
        result is read as `ended=<yes|no>`: yes when both recorded pids are gone after `close_host`.
    - **R5a:** `host_adopt` runs `viola --home <home> adopt <id> --name adopt-probe --parent r5-parent --model
      <model> --effort <effort>` from `<base>/typed-in`. The script waits on the instance's `events.ndjson` for the
      `session-start` line, within a bound under 120 s. It reads:
      - the snapshot's `lineage.parent`;
      - its `launch` pair;
      - the line's `cause` and `agent_session_id`.

      It sends the one compiled prompt (below) through `viola send adopt-probe` (stdin) and waits up to 300 s through
      `viola wait` for `turn-ended`. Then `close_host` runs.
    - **R5a's grant parameters (`inputs#I2` (2)), beside the home:**
      - **The prompt, one compiled literal in the script:** `Reply with the single word: adopted`. One send, no
        other text typed.
      - **Model and effort:** `haiku` and `low`, the cheapest pair the CLI takes (`--effort` takes low · medium ·
        high · xhigh · max). They are handed on the resumed child's argv as every start hands them. Whether the
        session runs on them is unmeasured (architecture · decision/launch-pair-handed-not-verified), and the
        verdict reads only the pair the snapshot recorded. They are the arm's `<model>` and `<effort>` arguments
        (the entry's `R5_MODEL` / `R5_EFFORT`), so his grant can name another pair.
      - **What the turn spends:** one model turn on that pair. Its input is the resumed session's whole transcript
        plus the prompt, so the cost scales with the session he adopts. A probe session of one short exchange keeps
        it to a few thousand input tokens and an output of about one word. The automatic verify's starts are spent
        only in an unstamped home (his home choice). His own plain start and its first exchange are his, outside the
        script.
    - **R5b:** `host_adopt` runs `viola --home <home> adopt <id> --name adopt-live --json`. It reads `session-live`
      (exit 1 through `script -e`) and no `adopt-live` child (no `child_pid` recorded), and spends no model turn.
    - **Teardown:** the `trap` above ends every process the script started and nothing else. Nothing is removed
      recursively: the base is named on stdout for the operator.
    - **Verdict lines** (the plan's closed set; verification-harness.md 2026-11-24):
      - `r5a: <green|red> resumed=<yes|no> lineage=<yes|no> pair=<model>/<effort>|unread turn=<ended|none|unfired>
        ended=<yes|no>`;
      - `r5b: <green|red> refused=<session-live|<code>|none> started=<none|child> ended=<yes|no>`.

      A line is green only when every field reads its first word and `pair` equals the granted pair.
    - **Rehearsal:** builds a fake-only PATH (`<base>/bin` holding a copy of `target/debug/viola-fake-agent` as
      `claude`, then `/usr/bin:/bin` alone, so mise's `claude` is unreachable). It stamps its own `<base>/home` with
      `viola verify` against that fake under a test-owned user home and runtime dir, as the harness boot does
      (verification-harness.md §boot). It plants the fake's `fake-args` for a turn end, and for R5b `agents-rows.json`
      listing the minted id. It runs both arms through the same `host_adopt` and `close_host` (R5a with `haiku` and
      `low`), prints both lines with their `ended=` read, then prints `r5: rehearsed — not a live reading` last.
      It cannot reach a real `claude` or the operator's sessions.

13. **R5 itself** (the operator pass, on his word only, at his host, unlocked). `cargo build -p viola` (entry 20)
    builds the release-shaped binary. Then:
    - entry 21 (R5a), with `R5_HOME`, `R5_ID`, `R5_MODEL` and `R5_EFFORT` exported: his home choice, the id of the
      plain session he started and ended himself, and the pair he grants (`haiku` / `low` unless he names another);
    - entry 22 (R5b), with `R5_ID` the id of a plain session he leaves running.

    Each verdict line is copied by the operator into `evidence/r5.md`, which entry 14 reads. The home is his choice
    (Block 1, R5a): his stamped `~/.viola` adds no verify starts and leaves `adopt-probe` on his board; a fresh scratch
    home spends the automatic verify's starts.

body:
# Implement directive — «`viola adopt`» (chunk 2026-11-24-viola-adopt)

The plan is approved (P5 card 2, plan rev 4). This window is fresh: read the chunk's documents from the store and
its evidence dir from disk first. This directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

**In your own chat messages never print a compiled screen literal verbatim**: name it. Call no scheduled-wake or
timer tool. **NO mutation run and NO witness run. NO window of the real compositor is opened, moved, focused or
closed, NO key is sent, NO real `claude` is started, NO signal goes to a process this run did not start, and NO
real session of the operator's is read, listed, ended, adopted or resumed by this run — R5 is not this run's:
`scripts/r5-adopt.sh` runs ONLY in its `--rehearse` form. `viola adopt` itself runs ONLY under a test-owned home
with the fake agent as `claude`.** Nothing of the
operator's real `~/.claude*` is read; no `viola list` runs with a real `claude` reachable on its PATH.

## The host — another project works here

- The filtered entries run as they come. **Before the three whole layers (unit, integration, e2e) and again before
  `pre-push`: read `hostwatch.py read --last 15`** (`~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py`)
  and `df -m /tmp` beside it. QUIET → go on. CONTENDED naming a NEIGHBOUR alive in the stalled seconds → STOP and
  say in one line which entries wait; the overseer arranges a quiet window. A CONTENDED reading where only this
  run's own build was alive is none: go on.
- A gate red where no assertion failed on a value (a stall, a timeout, a kill) is read against the same record
  first and never re-run for green into a contended host: say so and wait for the overseer's word.

## Stops

- **The plan's order is the order.** The rehearsal entry is fired once the script exists and BEFORE any graded
  use: read with your own eyes that its PATH holds the fake `hyprctl`, `foot` and `claude` first and that no line
  of it can reach `/usr/bin/hyprctl` — say how you read it. A rehearsal that reached the real compositor is a
  stop, reported at once.
- **The four controls** (`adopt-live`, `adopt-shape`, `adopt-order`, `adopt-parent`) are fired by `gate.py control` with the
  plan's `--timeout` on the entries the plan names for them. A case that cannot be made to fail with its guard removed stops
  implement for that site.
- **No new closed word, exit, flag, request, time bound, environment read, record field, MCP tool or fake mode
  beyond the plan's, and no path in `adopt` or its script that ends or signals a process viola did not start:** a need for any stops implement and is the operator's — he is away, so it is written to the
  run's `founder-forks.md` with its options priced and the step stops there.
- A filter that still selects 0 tests after its step is a red, said so. A sweep of a counted literal (the help's
  rows, the exit-cause table's row count, the `detail` enum, the per-verb document tables) reads the test tree's
  strings too.
- A red that would move a plan entry stops implement before the operator pass: say which entry and why.
- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are. Remove no scratch clone or test dir by a recursive delete: name it in the report.
- Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home and runtime dir, and every test ends the stand-in terminal
  and the wrapper it started. No leaf gains a figure the code states. No master row is reworded in this skill.

## On green — the operator pass, WITHOUT R5

Write the chunk report (P4), saying plainly what stands unproven behind R5 and behind the operator's forks W1 to
W4. Then run the operator pass in this same window: `pre-push`, hygiene, the pre-CI commit and push, the CI read
(`ci.py conclusion`, leg=operator). **Fire none of the entries that belong to R5 (its build, R5a, R5b): each
waits on the operator's own word, which has not been given. The `ci-fold` entry reads the two renamed cases'
times from THIS push's CI run and writes `evidence/ci-fold.md`.** Write the pass's record as it stands, R5 unfired, the gated entry
deferred, and end the turn with one line: the CI verdict, the rehearsal's verdict line, and what is left on disk
outside the tree, each by name. End every process you start.

**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-24T11-08-28Z-wrap/
- NEVER claim WCAG conformance for the cli or the `viola run` TUI, whether `viola run`, a passed `viola revive` or a passed `viola adopt` started it.

- NEVER block, refuse or delay a human keystroke in `viola run`, or in a start a passed `viola revive` or a passed `viola adopt` made, past the current paste's in-flight chunk and closing marker (the one exception: a start's automatic verify window, before any child exists, where a typed key waits in the terminal's own buffer until the child starts), and never count focus / mouse / resize sequences or terminal replies as editing (P4).

- Eight time bounds viola holds (wait timeout and cap, MCP call deadline, dialog hold, send readiness gate, paste write, confirmation windows, agents read, the start's Claude config lock wait) fall on the driver, viola's child or viola's own start; no key is blocked, refused or delayed by them (provisional). The start's verify stop grace, the wait before a stopped start's verify child is killed, likewise falls on viola's own child only: no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it and the wheel is untouched. An MCP frame tool call (send, wait, last, answer) that outlives the MCP call deadline (`viola_mcp::MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`) ends `instance-unreachable` / `call-deadline`, the outcome of a send unknown; only the MCP frame tools write that detail, never the CLI, whose exit-21 cause set stays six. The one `claude agents --json` read `viola list`, `viola revive` and `viola adopt` each make (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is killed at 5 s, a bound on viola's own child only: a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open, and no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. `viola wait` returns `{timed_out:true}` only for a timeout the caller passes in. The MCP `wait` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) clamps its `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP`, also its default when the caller passes none (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`), so an MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` at `WAIT_CAP`: a bound on the driver only (the hidden, plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving Claude session, never a person), no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. A raised dialog takes a `viola answer` only within the dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, PROVISIONAL bounds; chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver); at the hold's end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line, the dialog renders for the human in the `claude` TUI, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog` (exit 13) — the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed; a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`. Once typed, a confirmed `viola send` waits for its confirmation within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI within its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL, architecture [Delivery Confirmation]); a send not confirmed inside its window is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`: a bound on the driver only, the confirm wait takes no key and blocks, refuses or delays none, and the wheel is untouched. A start's window step waits at most 5 s for its own terminal's window to appear in the compositor's client list, each compositor read through the Hyprland seam is bounded at 5 s a reply (the window step, viola open, viola focus), and viola open waits at most 30 s for the instance it started to come live, then reads not-live; each falls on viola's own start or verb, never on a key typed into a session, and never moves the wheel.

- cli: no interactive prompt, pager or redraw, and input is stdin / `--file` only; tui: once the child starts the terminal belongs to the child, and viola writes zero bytes of its own to it (only a start's automatic verify lines L1 to L5 and verify's own output precede the child's bytes) (under `viola revive --json` or `viola adopt --json` a `pump_child` error prints no document: viola writes nothing past it, and a peer the wrapper refuses is dropped in `accept_loop`, before its worker thread and any frame: it writes nothing to the outer terminal and moves no wheel), and once the wrapped child holds the terminal, human keystrokes are never blocked, refused or dropped: queued with the paste in arrival order, they wait behind at most its in-flight chunk and closing marker (the one exception is a start's automatic verify window, before the child starts: a key typed then waits in the terminal's own buffer), and focus / mouse / resize sequences and terminal replies (F-W2's closed list) are never counted as editing; every other byte is. viola has no web or graphical frontend; the terminal fleet console's keyboard reach is the route entry «Fleet a11y verification»'s.

- On the CLI, state is always a printed word (`stale`, `DIALOG <kind>`, `expired`, `unverified-cli`, the STATUS words `idle` / `busy` on joined wrapped rows and the unwrapped rows' `n/a` cells; on a terminal too narrow only an unwrapped NAME is cut, to the column less 3 characters plus `...` and never inside a `\xHH` escape, a wrapped NAME never, and piped output and `--json` keep every name whole); colour is a second cue only (amber SGR only on `DIALOG`, dim on stale rows, bold only on NAME values, always beside the word), `unable` / `fail` are never coloured, and viola emits no SGR of its own under non-TTY / `NO_COLOR` (an empty value included) / `TERM=dumb` / `--json` / a passthrough role / `viola run` / a passed `viola revive` / a passed `viola adopt`, and `viola link` / `viola unlink` print one plain-ASCII result line in one write with no SGR in any mode, and `viola up` prints one line per instance, `<name>  <word>` or `<name>  live  <placement>`, plain ASCII, with no SGR, each line in one write. viola has no web or graphical frontend, so no page token pair or layout to verify.

- Env vars: `VIOLA_` prefix (`VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR`, `VIOLA_BIN`) — wrapper-to-child plumbing only, never configuration. Test-harness-only variables (`AGENT_RUN_RIG` and `CI` among them, never read by `viola`) use `AGENT_RUN_` (`AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED` — read by `viola-harness`, the root test chain `tests/support/home.rs` and/or viola-e2e's `tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` `Booted` guard and `harness::session` guard (`HarnessSession`'s `Drop`, through `keep_home`, which reads both `KEEP_*` variables) and are never read by `viola`. Besides `PATH` (read and set for the child) and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (read only, for the socket directory) and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (its value read by `viola verify`, and by the `viola run`, `viola revive` and `viola adopt` start, only when `claude_env_keep` keeps that name, to locate the Claude config file), two of the ratified exceptions are the test seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (u64 ms capped at 5 000; security-plan Decisions Log 2026-09-27) and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (fires only on exactly `1`, a forced fail-open `hook` panic; Decisions Log 2026-09-28), neither prefix: each read only by a `viola` built with the `fake-agent` feature, absent from release builds, configuring nothing. A third, in every build: `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM`, the terminal's own names, read (never set) only by viola's colour layer (`src/human/style.rs`, `viola list`'s human mode) to decide whether and how deep its SGR bytes are written — never echoed, configuring nothing, disabling no control and widening no redaction (the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline; arch §Occupied Resources → Environment variables).

- CLI exit codes: 0 · 1 (a `cli` verb's internal error: `error: internal error` on stderr, or under `--json` before a `--` the catch site's `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr then empty, `run`, `revive`'s start, `adopt`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` silent at that site; also `viola run`'s and `viola revive`'s start, and `viola verify`, refusing the home tree before any log opens: the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or the instance-state pair for an instance-level refusal, no line written, no child started; also `viola run`'s, `viola revive`'s and `viola adopt`'s start refusing the socket directory (`socket_dir_ready`, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a failed create and a refused check read this one code, a `Server::bind` failure does not): the stderr `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or under `viola revive --json` the `socket-dir-refused` document, and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, no path, pid or uid; `viola verify`'s refusals each carry their code on the `process-exit` it writes under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`: `program-not-found` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `version-unreadable` · `strict-modes-failed` · `unclean-fixture`, beside `interrupted`; a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, yet `viola verify` still exits 1 on a failed relied row with that row's stamp written, and `verify` takes no `--json`; also `viola open`'s refusals, `strict-modes-failed` before any log, `already-live`, `stale-heartbeat`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `terminal-not-found`, `not-live` or `internal-error`, each under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document; also `viola adopt`'s refusals, under `--json` one refusal document whose `<code>` is one of `strict-modes-failed` · `session-live` · `already-live` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error` (`session-live` when a `claude agents --json` row carries the adopted id); also `viola focus`'s and `viola up`'s refusals, each an `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr with no path, or under `--json` one refusal document (`viola up`'s `boot-time-unread`, `strict-modes-failed`, `pinned-hash-mismatch` or `terminal-not-found`); also a `viola up` whose lines are not all successes) · 2 (usage error, and `viola send` text over 16 MiB or not UTF-8) · 10 human-typing · 11 unassigned (the retired `budget-paused` refusal's code, never reused or renumbered) · 12 unverified-cli · 13 not-delivered · 14 unknown · 20 wrapper fault (a `-32602` from `link` / `unlink` included) · 21 instance unreachable (under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, written by `client::unreachable_document` (the board builds its own), `<cause>` one of the six exit-21 words of `viola_core::UnreachableCause`'s closed seven (the seventh, `call-deadline`, written by the MCP frame tools alone) `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`, no `RefusalReason`; with no live endpoint `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint` reads an instance directory as `instance-dead` and anything else as `unwrapped-name`, so a stale instance reads `instance-dead`, and a wrapper lost with the call open reads `endpoint-lost`; also, on `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, a server that is not the recorded wrapper — a connected peer whose euid is not this user's or cannot be read (`peer_admitted`), or the connected peer's pid or OS start time not the snapshot's, or that check not made — no frame written, `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` under `--json` (Linux only; the Windows and macOS legs left with their code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`), after the client's own exit-13 refusals, the strict-modes instance check and the socket-directory check, with no exit code or `RefusalReason` of its own, its `--json` word the document's `detail`; also `viola list`'s refused strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance, which refuses the whole board, no log opened, and `viola up`'s same board refusal (`instance-unreachable`, `strict-modes-failed`), with no line printed; also `viola focus`'s refused strict-modes check: the `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` under `--json` with stderr empty, nothing under the home opened and no line written; and `viola plugin install`'s refused strict-modes check of the home or an existing `marketplace/` tree dir, nothing created, no log opened; and the refused instance check of `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` (the target instance) and of `viola link` / `viola unlink` (the driven instance), made first by `client::refuse_untrusted` (`check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`, after `send`'s text read, before any connect, role file or log opens): the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` under `--json`, no log opened, no line written; and, on those same eight verbs, past that check and before any connect, a refused socket directory on the recorded endpoint (`check_endpoint_dir` in `client::connect`): the socket-directory hint last on stderr, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` under `--json`, one `process-exit` at WARN with `during` `connect` and no `channel-request`); `viola hook` always 0. `viola revive` exits 0, 1 for a refused strict-modes check (ahead of the wrapper log: the stderr pair, no log line) or a preflight refusal (`already-live` or `stale-heartbeat` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing`, read in that order, each one `process-exit` line) or a refusal of the start after a passed preflight, or 2 for a usage error; it takes `--json` on both arms, where a refused strict-modes check and every refusal of its start is instead one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`, by `client::refused_document`; a `claude` not on `PATH` or an anyhow error of the start is `internal-error`), stderr empty, exit 1, and `<name> --list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order (a `pump_child` error prints no document: the child has held the terminal).

- Arguments mirror channel params: `viola send <target>` (text from stdin or `--file`), `viola wait <target> [--after <cursor>] [--timeout-ms <n>]`, `viola last <target>`, `viola answer <target> <dialog_id>` (response JSON from stdin/`--file`), `viola pause <target>`, `viola release <target>` (a `--budget` flag is a usage error, exit 2), `viola link|unlink <driver> <driven>`; `viola open <name> [--parent <name>] [--role overseer|builder|worker] [--cwd <dir>] [--workspace N] [--model M] [--effort E] [--json] -- claude`; `viola adopt <SESSION_ID> --name <NAME> [--parent <NAME>] [--model <MODEL>] [--effort <EFFORT>] [--json]` takes the id in the closed session-id shape, hex of either case, and no words after `--` (a `--parent` equal to `--name` a usage error, exit 2); `viola focus <name> [--json]` takes one ViolaName and `--json` only; `viola up [<NAME>...] [--dry-run] [--json]` re-opens, after a reboot, each instance gone before the boot through `viola revive` in a new terminal (names given narrow the fleet, a name not scanned reads `not-taken`; CLI-only, no MCP tool and no channel method); `viola revive <name> [--id <ID>] [--fork] [--model <MODEL>] [--effort <EFFORT>] [-- <child args>]` and `viola revive <name> --list` send no channel frame (`--list` conflicts with `--id`, `--fork`, `--model`, `--effort`, the hidden `--origin` and the trailing arguments; under the hidden `--origin <cli|agent>`, which takes no `--place`, the revive places its window on the workspace a real snapshot recorded); `viola run --parent <NAME>` declares the instance's parent (one equal to its own name a usage error, exit 2, before anything is read; with no `--parent` an inherited `VIOLA_NAME` is taken as parent only, dropped when it equals the own name) and `viola run --role <WORD>` its role, a code word; `viola run --model <MODEL>` names the model handed to the child, a model word, and `viola run --effort <EFFORT>` its effort, one of the five effort words, a value failing its shape a usage error, exit 2, and with none given each is the `config.json` default, else the compiled default; the hidden `viola run --origin <WORD>` names the window's origin, an origin word (any other word a usage error, exit 2), and the hidden `viola run --place <N>` the workspace the window is moved to (`--place` without `--origin` a usage error, exit 2).

- `config.json` is parsed tolerantly (unknown keys skipped and counted) and carries `v`; keys: `diagnostics_level` (`info` by default, or `debug`; the only source of the process-log level, `RUST_LOG` having no effect; obs D-15), `claude_env_keep` (the R8 pass-list of `CLAUDE*` names, an array of at most 32 names each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`, default empty; a bad value is rejected whole, and an identity-floor name in it has no effect; keeping `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` makes `viola verify`, `viola run`, `viola revive` and `viola adopt` read its value to locate the Claude config file), `dialog_hold_s` (the dialog hold as a `DialogHold`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, read once at the wrapper's start; any other value takes 60 with one `parse-rejected` line, so no value makes the hold zero or unbounded), `verify_new_cli` (a JSON boolean, default false, turning on the `viola run` / `viola revive` start's automatic verify of a claude version with no attempted stamps entry; any other value reads false with one `parse-rejected` config-json `malformed` line), `default_model` (a string of the model word shape, default the model half of `DEFAULT_PAIR`) and `default_effort` (one of the five effort words, default the effort half of `DEFAULT_PAIR`), each bad value taking that half with one `parse-rejected` config-json `malformed` line, and no value disabling a control.

The only crate that knows Claude Code (test-only exceptions: the live rig in `viola-e2e` reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload and the cachedChromeExtensionInstalled key name, never a value, and its own captured StopFailure payload's key names, error word (one of the CLI's 13, else `other`) and two text lengths, never a text, and seeds its private Claude config; VH reads the real config's key names and a needle, never a value; the fake agent and the rig read a config's trust record). It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`.
