- `viola adopt`'s start is no `cli` verb: it logs as process `run` into `run-<name>.ndjson` through run's own lines and spans, adding no event, detail word, field, subject or span of its own. `viola revive`'s start arm logs as process `run` once its instance check has passed (`run-<name>.ndjson`, each preflight refusal — `already-live` (a live holder or a fresh replayed beat), `stale-heartbeat` (a stale holder), `no-session`, `session-live`, `cwd-missing` — one `process-exit{exit_code:1, detail}`; `viola adopt`'s preflight likewise ends one `process-exit{exit_code:1, detail:"session-live"}` with no child started; its `session-live` reading (and `viola adopt`'s start's, alike), skipped under revive's `--fork` and passing on a failed read, writes one `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"agents-probe"}` pair there, plus one `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json"}` on an oversize or malformed answer); `viola revive --list` is role `cli` (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract; the sixth exemption retired): after its strict-modes check passes and only under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` it writes `process-start` / `process-exit` (`exit_code` 0 with no detail; `exit_code` 1 `detail:"no-session"` on an empty chain) into the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson`, with no name no log, and its dispatch `Err` or panic reaches the `cli` catch site. A refused instance check on either `viola revive` arm (start or `--list`) or on `viola adopt`'s start, or `viola mcp`'s refused `viola_state::strict::check_path` of its home or `diagnostics/` (run before its `mcp` role file opens; exit 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr), or `viola plugin install`'s refused `check_path` of its home or a `marketplace/` tree dir (run before its `cli` role file opens; exit 21, the stderr pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), or `viola link` / `viola unlink`'s refused `check_instance` of the driven instance (run before their `cli` role file opens; exit 21, the fixed instance-state pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), opens no role file and writes no line (the seventh exemption). So does a refused strict-modes check on the hook event and dialog paths (exit 0, nothing printed), on `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release` or `viola focus` (exit 21, the instance pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), on `viola verify`'s home tree (exit 1, the home pair) or on the home tree of `viola run`, `viola revive`'s start arm or `viola adopt`'s start (exit 1, the home or the instance pair) (the eighth exemption). A refused peer euid (Unix) or a failed server check (the peer pid and start-time comparison, run on Linux, the one target) sends no frame and opens no `channel.request`: the eight CLI frame verbs (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`; `link` / `unlink` into the driven instance's `cli-<driven>.ndjson`) end `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside their dispatch span with no `channel-request` line; `viola hook` writes `hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}` at WARN (on a dialog hook `hook-invoked{corr:null}` first, then `decision_emitted:false`); MCP's frame tools return `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and no line, as their refused `check_endpoint_dir` (made after `live_endpoint`) does with `detail` `socket-dir-refused` and no frame, and as the liveness pre-check's does with `without_endpoint`'s reading (`instance-dead` or `unwrapped-name`) and as their own refused `check_instance` of the home and the instance directory does (made before `live_endpoint`, `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, no frame), and as `send`, `wait`, `last` and `answer` do at the MCP call deadline, `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE` (`detail` `call-deadline`, a cause the MCP frame tools alone write and the CLI never does; the frame dropped); no pid, start time, path or endpoint in any line. A `release` whose `from` is not a string or that carries any budget key (true, false, a string or null) is a plain `-32602` (data null) after the release-from-driver check, with no `release-from-driver` line, no wheel moved and no record; its `channel-response` carries `detail` `invalid-params` on both sides at WARN. The implicit link record on a `send` or an `answer`, the explicit `link` / `unlink` methods the driven wrapper serves (their trace the call's `channel-request` / `channel-response` pair, which holds neither name), the link set's restore at start and the replay's link rule carry no span and no process-log line of their own; `driver`, `driven` and `since` reach no home-level line; a start's `parent` and `role` names reach no process-log or detail line (only `events.ndjson`, the snapshot, the `viola list` board, `list --json` and the MCP list result). The lineage line and the launch line written at every run, revive and adopt start, and the window line a start under `--origin` writes after its launch line, are events-log product audit data: each wakes no wait and opens no span, writes no process-log line and no terminal byte of its own. The wrapper's stdin typed mark and its held scheduled-wakes count are in-memory state that open no span and write no line of their own, and carry no key and no prompt text. The cut mark a cut paste leaves is in-memory wrapper state too: it opens no span and writes no line of its own, its set showing as the cut send's `send-refused` `paste-cut` record and its clears as their own `prompt-submitted`, `session-start` and `session-end` records. The send's transcript echo read (the end offset before the paste and the tag count after it) opens no span and writes no line or span field of its own; its result shows only as the `send-confirmed` line inside `run.confirm_window`. A `send-refused` line carries `refusal`, `detail`, `side` and `wheel`, never `window`, `used_percentage`, `resets_at` or `paused`. At a dialog hold's end (`run.dialog_await`'s `deadline_ms`, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s` in ms, 60 000–3 600 000, default 60 000) the wrapper appends one `dialog-expired{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` product line and writes one `dialog-answered{corr:<dialog_id>, dialog_kind, deadline_hit:true, duration_ms}` with no `from` / `from_trust`; a hand-back or an answer writes neither; the hook then writes `hook-decision{decision_emitted:false, deadline_hit:false}`, `deadline_hit:true` only when its own read times out at its backstop bound `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s).
